```{r}
libs <- c("tidyverse", "here", "reshape2", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "vegan")

lapply(libs, library, character.only = T)

# ============================================================
# INPUT FILES AND WORKSHEETS
# ============================================================
# Update these inputs for another project with the same table structure.
abundance_path <- here::here("data_raw", "MCO_ASV_abundance_table.csv")
taxonomy_path <- here::here("data_raw", "MCO_LCA_taxonomy.csv")
metadata_path <- here::here("data_raw", "HS metadata.xlsx")

spider_sheet <- "HS spider"
web_sheet <- "HS web"
abdomen_sheet <- "HS abdomen"
asv_prefix <- "MCO_ASV_"

# ============================================================
# QUALITY-CONTROL SETTINGS

# Overall goal: retain biological samples and ASVs with
# sufficient read support, while removing weak detections
# and potential contamination.
#
# 1. min_cell_reads: Set low ASV read counts within
#    individual samples to zero.
# 2. min_sample_reads: Exclude biological samples with
#    insufficient total reads.
# 3. blank_asv_threshold: Identify ASVs with high read
#    counts in the negative-control blank for removal.
# 4. min_total_asv_reads: Exclude ASVs with insufficient
#    total reads across the retained biological samples.
#
# blank_pattern matches the shared blank naming format,
# ignoring case. Use the same pattern throughout the project.
# ============================================================

min_cell_reads <- 10
min_sample_reads <- 10000
blank_asv_threshold <- 100
min_total_asv_reads <- 100
blank_pattern <- "blank"

# ============================================================
# PLOT AND TEST SETTINGS
# ============================================================
# Number of named families shown separately; display grouping only.
number_of_top_families <- 25
# Spacing of rarefaction plotting points, not a filtering threshold.
rarefaction_step <- 500
# Maximum random starts; the main NMDS remains two-dimensional.
nmds_trymax <- 1000
# Reproducible NMDS fits and permutation tests.
analysis_seed <- 123
n_permutations <- 9999
# Formal group tests only; singleton groups remain in descriptive plots.
min_group_samples <- 2
# Run pairwise follow-up only when the overall PERMANOVA passes this level.
test_alpha <- 0.05
```
```{r}
# ===============================
# ABUNDANCE TABLE PROCESSING
# ===============================
# -------------------------------
# Read MCO abundance table
# -------------------------------

mco_HS <- read.csv(
  abundance_path,
  header = TRUE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Remove the sequencing suffix, e.g. _S385_L001_A_MCO.
mco_HS$SampleID <- gsub(
  "_S[0-9]+_L[0-9]+_[A-Z]_MCO$",
  "",
  mco_HS$SampleID
)

# Remove the trailing molecular ID, e.g. _M007143.
mco_HS$SampleID <- gsub(
  "_M[0-9]+$",
  "",
  mco_HS$SampleID
)

names(mco_HS)[names(mco_HS) == "SampleID"] <- "sample_id"

# ============================================================
# STEP 1: MERGE A/B/C SEQUENCING RECORDS
# ============================================================
#
# Each biological sample has three technical sequencing
# records: A, B, and C.
#
# Records with the same cleaned sample_id are grouped, and
# their MCO ASV read counts are summed.
#
# Output: one row per biological sample or blank.
# ============================================================

mco_HS_combined <- mco_HS %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      starts_with(asv_prefix),
      ~sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Identify blanks once from the cleaned, merged sample IDs.
blank_sample_ids <- mco_HS_combined$sample_id[
  str_detect(
    mco_HS_combined$sample_id,
    regex(blank_pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)
  )
]


# ============================================================
# STEP 2: REMOVE INDIVIDUAL ASV COUNTS BELOW 10 READS
# ============================================================
#
# Read counts below min_cell_reads are treated as low-count
# noise and converted to zero.
#
# This changes cell values but does not remove any samples
# or ASV columns.
# ============================================================

mco_HS_min10 <- mco_HS_combined %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      starts_with(asv_prefix),
      ~ifelse(.x < min_cell_reads, 0, .x)
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# STEP 3: CALCULATE TOTAL READS PER SAMPLE
# ============================================================
#
# Sample sequencing depth is recalculated after low-count
# ASV values have been converted to zero.
#
# sample_total_reads contains the sum of all remaining ASV
# reads in each sample.
# ============================================================

mco_HS_with_depth <- mco_HS_min10 %>%
  mutate(
    sample_total_reads = rowSums(
      across(starts_with(asv_prefix)),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# STEP 4: REMOVE LOW-DEPTH BIOLOGICAL SAMPLES
# ============================================================
#
# Biological samples must contain more than
# min_sample_reads total reads after low-count filtering.
# Later ASV and taxonomy filters can reduce this total;
# the sample-depth cutoff is not applied again.
#
# The HS blank is deliberately retained through this step
# so it can be used for contamination detection.
# ============================================================

mco_HS_depth_filtered <- mco_HS_with_depth %>%
  filter(
    sample_total_reads > min_sample_reads |
      sample_id %in% blank_sample_ids
  )


# ============================================================
# STEP 5: EXTRACT THE HS BLANK SAMPLE
# ============================================================
#
# The blank is separated from the biological samples so its
# ASV reads can be examined for possible contamination.
#
# sample_total_reads is removed because only the individual
# ASV counts are needed for contamination detection.
# ============================================================

blank_HS <- mco_HS_depth_filtered %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% blank_sample_ids) %>%
  select(-sample_total_reads)


# ============================================================
# STEP 6: IDENTIFY BLANK-ASSOCIATED ASVs
# ============================================================
#
# The blank table is converted from wide to long format.
#
# Reads are summed for each ASV across all blank samples.
# Although HS currently has one blank, this code also works
# if additional blanks are added later.
#
# ASVs with more than blank_asv_threshold reads in the
# blanks are classified as blank-associated ASVs.
# ============================================================

blank_asv_counts <- blank_HS %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(asv_prefix),
    names_to = "query",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(query) %>%
  summarise(
    total_blank_reads = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(total_blank_reads > blank_asv_threshold)

blank_asvs <- blank_asv_counts$query


# ============================================================
# STEP 7: REMOVE THE BLANK AND BLANK-ASSOCIATED ASVs
# ============================================================
#
# The blank has now been used for contamination detection
# and is removed from the biological dataset.
#
# ASV columns identified as blank-associated are also
# removed. any_of() allows the code to work even when no
# ASVs exceed the blank threshold.
# ============================================================

mco_HS_no_blank <- mco_HS_depth_filtered %>%
  filter(!sample_id %in% blank_sample_ids) %>%
  select(
    -sample_total_reads,
    -any_of(blank_asvs)
  )


# ============================================================
# STEP 8: CONVERT TO ASV-BY-SAMPLE FORMAT
# ============================================================
#
# The table currently has samples as rows and ASVs as
# columns.
#
# It is reshaped so that:
#   rows    = ASVs
#   columns = biological samples
#   values  = read counts
#
# query stores the ASV identifier and will later be used to
# merge the abundance and taxonomy tables.
# ============================================================

mco_HS_asv_by_sample <- mco_HS_no_blank %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(asv_prefix),
    names_to = "query",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sample_id,
    values_from = value
  )


# ============================================================
# STEP 9: APPLY THE FINAL ASV READ FILTER
# ============================================================
#
# Total reads are calculated for each ASV across all
# remaining biological samples.
#
# Only ASVs with more than min_total_asv_reads are retained.
# The resulting table is ready to merge with taxonomy using
# the query column.
# ============================================================

mco_HS_final <- mco_HS_asv_by_sample %>%
  mutate(
    asv_total_reads = rowSums(
      dplyr::select(., -query),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(asv_total_reads > min_total_asv_reads) %>%
  select(
    query,
    asv_total_reads,
    everything()
  )
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# TAXONOMIC TABLE PROCESSING
# ============================================================

mco_HS_tax <- read.csv(
  taxonomy_path,
  header = TRUE,
  sep = ",",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# FILTER TAXONOMIC ASSIGNMENTS
# ============================================================
#
# Length screening was completed upstream.
# Retain ASVs with Best_Identity >= 90.
# ============================================================
# Retain Arthropoda at the confirmed identity threshold.
# Preserve the original workflow's requirement for a
# non-missing Class assignment.
mco_HS_tax2 <- mco_HS_tax %>%
  filter(
    Best_Identity >= 90,
    Kingdom == "Metazoa",
    Phylum == "Arthropoda",
    !is.na(Class),
    Class != "Nan"
  )
# ============================================================
# APPLY TAXONOMIC CONFIDENCE THRESHOLDS
# ============================================================
#
# More specific taxonomic ranks require greater sequence
# identity:
#
#   Species: Best_Identity >= 98.5
#   Genus:   Best_Identity >= 95
#   Family:  Best_Identity >= 90
#
# These are the project's assignment thresholds.
# Labels below their rank's threshold are replaced with NA;
# this step does not remove ASVs.
# ============================================================

mco_HS_tax_final <- mco_HS_tax2 %>%
  mutate(
    Species = case_when(
      Best_Identity >= 98.5 ~ Species,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    Genus = case_when(
      Best_Identity >= 95 ~ Genus,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    Family = case_when(
      Best_Identity >= 90 ~ Family,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%

  # If species-level identification is unavailable but the
  # genus assignment is reliable, label it as "Genus sp".
  mutate(
    Species = ifelse(
      is.na(Species) & !is.na(Genus),
      paste(Genus, "sp"),
      Species
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# STANDARDIZE THE ASV IDENTIFIER
# ============================================================
#
# ASV_ID in the taxonomy table corresponds to query in the
# filtered abundance table.
# ============================================================

names(mco_HS_tax_final)[
  names(mco_HS_tax_final) == "ASV_ID"
] <- "query"


# ============================================================
# MERGE TAXONOMY WITH FILTERED ABUNDANCE
# ============================================================
#
# Only ASVs present in both the filtered taxonomy table and
# the filtered abundance table are retained.
# ============================================================

mco_HS_final_tax <- merge(
  mco_HS_tax_final,
  mco_HS_final,
  by = "query"
)

```

```{r filtering_summary_plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
# ============================================================
# FILTERING WORKFLOW SUMMARY
# ============================================================
#
# This section summarizes data retained after each major
# filtering stage.
#
# The figure contains separate panels for samples, ASVs,
# and reads because these quantities have very different
# scales.
# ============================================================


# Calculate total ASV reads in a sample-by-ASV table.
sum_asv_reads <- function(data) {

  asv_columns <- names(data)[
    startsWith(names(data), asv_prefix)
  ]

  sum(
    as.matrix(data[, asv_columns, drop = FALSE]),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
}

# Count ASVs with at least one non-zero read after each filtering step.
count_detected_asvs <- function(data) {
  asv_columns <- names(data)[startsWith(names(data), asv_prefix)]

  sum(
    colSums(
      as.matrix(data[, asv_columns, drop = FALSE]),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) > 0
  )
}

# Use the same stages for all three measurements.
workflow_stages <- c(
  "Initial data",
  "A/B/C records merged",
  "Counts below 10 set to zero",
  "Low-depth samples removed",
  "Blank and blank ASVs removed",
  "Low-total ASVs removed",
  "Taxonomy filtered and matched"
)


# Record the amount of data remaining after each stage.
filtering_summary <- bind_rows(

  tibble(
    metric = "Samples",
    stage = workflow_stages,
    remaining = c(
      n_distinct(mco_HS$sample_id),
      nrow(mco_HS_combined),
      nrow(mco_HS_min10),
      nrow(mco_HS_depth_filtered),
      nrow(mco_HS_no_blank),
      nrow(mco_HS_no_blank),
      nrow(mco_HS_no_blank)
    )
  ),

tibble(
  metric = "ASVs",
  stage = workflow_stages,
  remaining = c(
    count_detected_asvs(mco_HS),
    count_detected_asvs(mco_HS_combined),
    count_detected_asvs(mco_HS_min10),
    count_detected_asvs(mco_HS_depth_filtered),
    count_detected_asvs(mco_HS_no_blank),
    nrow(mco_HS_final),
    nrow(mco_HS_final_tax)
  )
),

  tibble(
    metric = "Reads",
    stage = workflow_stages,
    remaining = c(
      sum_asv_reads(mco_HS),
      sum_asv_reads(mco_HS_combined),
      sum_asv_reads(mco_HS_min10),
      sum_asv_reads(mco_HS_depth_filtered),
      sum_asv_reads(mco_HS_no_blank),
      sum(mco_HS_final$asv_total_reads, na.rm = TRUE),
      sum(mco_HS_final_tax$asv_total_reads, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )
) %>%

  mutate(
    metric = factor(
      metric,
      levels = c("Samples", "ASVs", "Reads")
    ),
    stage = factor(
      stage,
      levels = workflow_stages
    )
  ) %>%

  arrange(metric, stage) %>%

  group_by(metric) %>%

  mutate(
    previous = lag(remaining),
    removed = ifelse(
      is.na(previous),
      0,
      previous - remaining
    ),

    plot_label = ifelse(
      removed > 0,
      paste0(
        scales::comma(remaining),
        "\n(-",
        scales::comma(removed),
        ")"
      ),
      scales::comma(remaining)
    )
  ) %>%

  ungroup() %>%
  select(-previous)


print(filtering_summary, n = Inf, width = Inf)


# Create one summary visualization.
# Plot retained samples, ASVs, and reads in separate panels.
data_loss_plot <- ggplot(
  filtering_summary,
  aes(x = stage, y = remaining, fill = metric)
) +
  # Bar heights represent the amount of data remaining.
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +

  # Display retained counts and losses above each bar.
  geom_text(
    aes(label = plot_label),
    vjust = -0.25,
    size = 3.2,
    lineheight = 0.95
  ) +

  # Stack the three panels vertically.
  # Each panel has its own y-axis scale.
  facet_wrap(
    ~ metric,
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Samples" = "#2C7FB8",
      "ASVs" = "#31A354",
      "Reads" = "#756BB1"
    )
  ) +

  # Wrap long stage names onto multiple lines.
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 18)
  ) +

  # Reduce tick density and reserve space above the bars.
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.45))
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Data retained across the HS MCO filtering workflow",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Labels show data remaining;",
      "values in parentheses show loss from the previous stage."
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Data remaining",
    caption = paste(
      "Initial sample count represents unique cleaned sample IDs.",
      "A/B/C sequencing records are treated as technical records.",
      "Sample counts include blanks until blank removal.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +

  theme(
    legend.position = "none",

    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      hjust = 0.5,
      size = 9
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),

    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.8, "cm"),

    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 12
    ),

    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9)
  )

data_loss_plot
``` 

```{r}
# ============================================================
#install.packages("openxlsx")   # Run once
library(openxlsx)
# ============================================================
# READ METADATA FOR THE WEB ANALYSIS
# ============================================================
# HS spider provides host-spider identification.
# HS web provides the biological IDs associated with web samples.
# Keep the raw metadata tables unchanged; prepare analysis tables below.

# Read each worksheet as a separate table. Keep as raw input.
hs_spider_raw  <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(metadata_path, sheet = spider_sheet)
hs_web_raw     <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(metadata_path, sheet = web_sheet)
hs_abdomen_raw <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(metadata_path, sheet = abdomen_sheet)

```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# PREPARE HOST SPIDER IDENTITY TABLE
# ============================================================
# Input:
#   Raw host-spider records from the "HS spider" worksheet.
#
# Output:
#   spider_identity
#   One row per biological spider.
#
# This table stores the host spider identity used to group
# web samples in the downstream analysis.
# Retain morphological, molecular and tentative identifications.
# ============================================================
spider_identity <- hs_spider_raw %>%

  transmute(

    biological_id =
      str_squish(as.character(Sample.ID)),

    morphology_id =
      na_if(
        str_squish(as.character(Morphology.ID)),
        ""
      ),

    molecular_id =
      na_if(
        str_squish(as.character(Molecular.ID)),
        ""
      ),

    tentative_species_id =
      na_if(
        str_squish(as.character(Tentative.Species.ID)),
        ""
      )
  ) %>%

  filter(
    str_detect(biological_id, "^HS[0-9]+$")
  )

```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# PREPARE METADATA FOR QC-RETAINED WEB SAMPLES
# ============================================================
# The HS spider and HS web sheets share biological IDs.
# Convert each biological ID to its web-sample ID:
# HS1 -> hw1. Use the actual ID, not the row number.

web_analysis_metadata <- spider_identity %>%
  mutate(
    sample_id = str_replace(biological_id, "^HS", "hw")
  )

# Keep the QC-retained sample set and attach host information.
mco_HS_sample_metadata <- mco_HS_no_blank %>%
  distinct(sample_id) %>%
  left_join(
    web_analysis_metadata,
    by = "sample_id"
  )

```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# CREATE THE ANALYSIS-READY LONG TABLE
# ============================================================
# Inputs:
#   mco_HS_final_tax: one row per ASV, with samples in columns.
#   mco_HS_sample_metadata: one row per QC-retained sample.
#
# Output:
#   One row per sample–ASV combination, including zero reads.

analysis_sample_ids <- mco_HS_sample_metadata$sample_id

mco_HS_analysis_long <- mco_HS_final_tax %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(analysis_sample_ids),
    names_to = "sample_id",
    values_to = "reads"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    mco_HS_sample_metadata,
    by = "sample_id"
  )

# Each sample–ASV combination must occur only once.
stopifnot(
  anyDuplicated(
    mco_HS_analysis_long[c("sample_id", "query")]
  ) == 0
)

# Summarize the final analysis dataset.
analysis_table_summary <- mco_HS_analysis_long %>%
  summarise(
    number_of_rows = n(),
    number_of_samples = n_distinct(sample_id),
    number_of_asvs = n_distinct(query),
    number_of_host_groups = n_distinct(tentative_species_id),
    total_reads = sum(reads)
  )

print(analysis_table_summary, width = Inf)
```

```{r hs_plot_setup}
# ============================================================
# SHARED DATA PREPARATION FOR WEB-COMMUNITY PLOTS
# ============================================================
#
# These plots describe the retained ASVs, not numbers of species or
# organisms. Host groups use `tentative_species_id`. Read counts
# reflect the sequencing data and must not be interpreted directly
# as organism abundance.
#
# Create the sample-by-ASV matrix once. Metadata remains in a
# separate table with one row per sample. The long table is retained
# for taxonomic summaries.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# REUSE THE FINAL LONG TABLE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Reuse the validated long table; do not apply another filter here.
mco_HS_plot_data <- mco_HS_analysis_long

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CREATE THE SAMPLE-BY-ASV MATRIX
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Rows = samples; columns = ASVs; cells = retained integer read counts.
community_wide <- mco_HS_plot_data %>%
  select(sample_id, query, reads) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = query,
    values_from = reads,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  arrange(sample_id)

community_matrix <- community_wide %>%
  select(-sample_id) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(community_matrix) <- community_wide$sample_id

# This protects the relative-abundance and distance calculations below.
# Do not silently remove a sample that becomes empty after taxonomic filtering.
stopifnot(all(rowSums(community_matrix) > 0))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PREPARE SAMPLE METADATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

analysis_sample_metadata <- mco_HS_plot_data %>%
  distinct(sample_id, biological_id, tentative_species_id)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DEFINE CONSISTENT HOST ORDER, COLORS AND LABELS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Count samples once. Order hosts by decreasing sample size, with
# alphabetical ties. This order is shared by all host-group figures.
host_sample_counts <- analysis_sample_metadata %>%
  count(tentative_species_id, name = "number_of_samples") %>%
  arrange(desc(number_of_samples), as.character(tentative_species_id))

host_levels <- as.character(host_sample_counts$tentative_species_id)

# Setting factor levels here also fixes facet and legend order after joins.
analysis_sample_metadata <- analysis_sample_metadata %>%
  mutate(
    tentative_species_id = factor(tentative_species_id, levels = host_levels)
  )

host_sample_counts <- host_sample_counts %>%
  mutate(
    tentative_species_id = factor(tentative_species_id, levels = host_levels)
  )

host_colors <- setNames(
  grDevices::hcl.colors(length(host_levels), palette = "Dark 3"),
  host_levels
)

# Group-comparison labels show how many individual web samples contribute.
host_labels <- setNames(
  paste0(host_levels, " (n=", host_sample_counts$number_of_samples, ")"),
  host_levels
)

# With coord_flip(), reverse the displayed x-axis limits so the canonical
# host order reads top to bottom. Vertical plots read left to right;
# facets and legends follow host_levels without this display reversal.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE SAMPLE-LEVEL DIVERSITY
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Observed richness counts positive ASV cells. Shannon uses natural logarithms
# and the proportions of ASV reads within each sample.
sample_alpha_diversity <- tibble(
  sample_id = rownames(community_matrix),
  retained_reads = as.numeric(rowSums(community_matrix)),
  observed_asvs = as.numeric(vegan::specnumber(community_matrix)),
  shannon_index = as.numeric(vegan::diversity(community_matrix, index = "shannon"))
) %>%
  left_join(analysis_sample_metadata, by = "sample_id")
```

### A. Sampling structure and coverage

```{r hs_host_counts, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 1: NUMBER OF WEB SAMPLES PER HOST GROUP
# ============================================================
#
# Main figure: sampling structure.
#
# Each bar counts web samples. This establishes how unevenly the
# host groups were sampled; a longer bar does not imply greater
# community diversity.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
host_sample_count_plot <- ggplot(
  host_sample_counts,
  aes(x = tentative_species_id, y = number_of_samples)
) +
  geom_col(
    fill = "#257C9D",
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = number_of_samples),
    hjust = -0.2
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = rev(host_levels)
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
```

```{r hs_read_rarefaction, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 2: READ-BASED RAREFACTION CURVES
# ============================================================
#
# Diagnostic figure: retained read-depth coverage.
#
# Each line is the expected number of retained ASVs in a random
# subsample of reads from one web sample. The x-axis counts retained
# Arthropoda reads, not original sequencing reads. No sample is
# replaced by a rarefied sample here.
#
# The prior <10-cell-read and >100-total-ASV filters removed rare
# detections. Therefore, these curves describe the filtered dataset
# and can look flatter than curves before those filters. They cannot
# establish completeness of the original biological community. A
# vegan warning about missing singletons is expected for this
# filtered input; do not interpret reads as animal counts.

# step controls the spacing of calculated plotting points only.
# It is not a filtering cutoff or a selected common rarefaction depth.
# rarecurve includes the full observed read total as each curve's endpoint.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE THE READ-BASED CURVES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
rarefaction_plot_data <- vegan::rarecurve(
  community_matrix,
  step = rarefaction_step,
  tidy = TRUE
) %>%
  rename(sample_id = Site, sampled_reads = Sample, expected_asvs = Species) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_id = as.character(sample_id)
  ) %>%
  left_join(analysis_sample_metadata, by = "sample_id")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
rarefaction_plot <- ggplot(
  rarefaction_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = sampled_reads,
    y = expected_asvs,
    group = sample_id,
    color = tentative_species_id
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.5,
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ tentative_species_id,
    ncol = 3
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = host_colors,
    breaks = host_levels
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(scale = 0.001, suffix = "k"),
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Read-based rarefaction of retained Arthropoda ASVs",
    subtitle = "One curve per web sample; all panels share axis scales",
    x = "Subsampled retained reads",
    y = "Expected retained ASVs",
    caption = "Curves are conditional on prior QC and taxonomic filtering."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "italic")
  )
```

```{r hs_sample_accumulation, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 3: SAMPLE ACCUMULATION CURVE
# ============================================================
#
# Exploratory figure: pooled sample coverage.
#
# This asks how many distinct ASVs are expected when combining more
# web samples. Its x-axis is the number of samples, unlike the
# read-based rarefaction above. The exact method averages over
# sample subsets; there is no arbitrary row-order effect. All
# retained host groups are pooled in this whole-dataset curve. The
# ribbon is plus/minus one conditional standard deviation, not a 95%
# CI. This curve does not extrapolate beyond the observed sample
# set. This is an exploratory coverage diagnostic, not a host-group
# comparison.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE EXPECTED SAMPLE ACCUMULATION
# ------------------------------------------------------------
accumulation_model <- vegan::specaccum(
  community_matrix,
  method = "exact",
  conditioned = TRUE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PREPARE THE ACCUMULATION PLOT TABLE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
accumulation_plot_data <- tibble(
  number_of_samples = accumulation_model$sites,
  expected_asvs = accumulation_model$richness,
  sd_asvs = accumulation_model$sd
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
accumulation_plot <- ggplot(
  accumulation_plot_data,
  aes(x = number_of_samples, y = expected_asvs)
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = pmax(0, expected_asvs - sd_asvs),
      ymax = pmin(ncol(community_matrix), expected_asvs + sd_asvs)
    ),
    fill = "#257C9D",
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_line(
    color = "#257C9D",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Accumulation of retained ASVs across web samples",
    subtitle = "All host groups pooled; exact expected accumulation",
    x = "Number of web samples",
    y = "Expected cumulative ASVs",
    caption = "Ribbon: mean +/- 1 conditional SD, clipped to the possible ASV range."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

accumulation_plot
```

```{r hs_group_accumulation, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 3A: SAMPLE ACCUMULATION WITHIN HOST GROUPS
# ============================================================
#
# Exploratory figure: sampling coverage within each host group.
#
# Use the same exact method as the pooled curve, separately for each
# host. Compare curves at the same number of samples: the endpoint
# of a longer curve also reflects greater sampling effort.
# Groups with one sample have one observed point, not a curve.
# Ribbons show one conditional SD, not confidence intervals.
#
# ASVs detected in every sample within a group have constant presence.
# This can trigger a zero-standard-deviation warning in specaccum().
# vegan handles the undefined correlations internally; retain these ASVs.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE EXPECTED ACCUMULATION FOR EACH HOST GROUP
# ------------------------------------------------------------
group_accumulation_data <- bind_rows(
  lapply(host_levels, function(host) {

    sample_ids <- analysis_sample_metadata$sample_id[
      analysis_sample_metadata$tentative_species_id == host
    ]
    group_matrix <- community_matrix[sample_ids, , drop = FALSE]

    if (length(sample_ids) == 1) {
      group_curve <- tibble(
        number_of_samples = 1,
        expected_asvs = as.numeric(vegan::specnumber(group_matrix)),
        sd_asvs = 0
      )
    } else {
      group_model <- vegan::specaccum(
        group_matrix,
        method = "exact",
        conditioned = TRUE
      )
      group_curve <- tibble(
        number_of_samples = group_model$sites,
        expected_asvs = group_model$richness,
        sd_asvs = group_model$sd
      )
    }

    group_curve %>%
      mutate(
        tentative_species_id = host,
        group_n = length(sample_ids),
        total_group_asvs = sum(colSums(group_matrix) > 0)
      )
  })
) %>%
  mutate(
    tentative_species_id = factor(tentative_species_id, levels = host_levels)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
group_accumulation_plot <- ggplot(
  group_accumulation_data,
  aes(
    x = number_of_samples,
    y = expected_asvs,
    color = tentative_species_id,
    group = tentative_species_id
  )
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = group_accumulation_data %>% filter(group_n > 1),
    aes(
      ymin = pmax(0, expected_asvs - sd_asvs),
      ymax = pmin(total_group_asvs, expected_asvs + sd_asvs),
      fill = tentative_species_id
    ),
    color = NA,
    alpha = 0.08,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = group_accumulation_data %>% filter(group_n > 1),
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = group_accumulation_data %>% filter(group_n == 1),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = host_colors,
    breaks = host_levels,
    labels = host_labels
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = host_colors) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Accumulation of retained ASVs within host groups",
    subtitle = "Exact expected accumulation; no extrapolation",
    x = "Number of web samples",
    y = "Expected cumulative ASVs",
    color = "Tentative host species",
    caption = paste(
      "Compare groups at equal sample counts. Singleton groups have one point.",
      "Ribbons: mean +/- 1 conditional SD, clipped to each group's observed ASV range.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )

group_accumulation_plot
```

```{r all_family_90, fig.width=11, fig.height=26}
# Count retained ASVs without a family assignment.
# These ASVs remain in mco_HS_final_tax but are not shown as named families.
missing_family_asvs <- mco_HS_final_tax %>%
  filter(is.na(Family) | trimws(Family) == "") %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(query)) %>%
  pull(n)

# Count distinct ASVs within each family.
family_counts_90 <- mco_HS_final_tax %>%
  filter(!is.na(Family), trimws(Family) != "") %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  summarise(
    Number_of_ASVs = n_distinct(query),
    .groups = "drop")

ggplot(
  family_counts_90,
  aes(
    x = Number_of_ASVs,
    y = reorder(Family, Number_of_ASVs)
  )
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#257C9D") +
  labs(
    title = "HS MCO: distinct ASVs by family",
    subtitle = "All retained classes; Best_Identity ≥90%",
    x = "Number of distinct ASVs",
    y = "Family",
    caption = paste0(
      "ASVs pooled across retained biological samples; not species counts or read abundance.\n",
      missing_family_asvs,
      " retained ASVs have no family assignment and are excluded from these bars."
    )
```

```{r hs_family_composition, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 7: FAMILY COMPOSITION BY HOST GROUP
# ============================================================
#
# Main figure: taxonomic composition.
#
# Each stacked bar shows the mean number of detected ASVs per web sample
# in a host group, split by Family. Every sample has equal weight within
# its host group, including samples with zero detections of a Family.
# These are ASV counts, not percentages, read counts or animal counts.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DEFINE THE DISPLAY SETTING
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Top N determines which named families get separate colors; it is not
# a QC threshold. Other named families are pooled only for display.
# No ASVs are removed from the long table or community matrix.
# number_of_top_families is defined in the initial settings.
# Unassigned family remains separate from the ranked named families.
# The same categories and colors are used in the read-composition plot.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# COUNT DETECTED ASVS AND COMPLETE SAMPLE-BY-FAMILY ZEROS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Count each ASV once if detected (reads > 0) in the sample.
# This summarizes detections; it does not filter the analysis dataset.
sample_family_asvs <- mco_HS_plot_data %>%
  mutate(
    Family_plot = if_else(
      is.na(Family) | str_squish(Family) == "",
      "Unassigned family",
      str_squish(Family)
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(sample_id, Family_plot) %>%
  summarise(
    number_of_asvs = n_distinct(query[reads > 0]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Include every retained sample for every Family, even if the input long
  # table stores only nonzero reads. For counts 5, 3 and absent, the mean
  # must be (5 + 3 + 0) / 3, not (5 + 3) / 2.
  tidyr::complete(
    sample_id = analysis_sample_metadata$sample_id,
    Family_plot,
    fill = list(number_of_asvs = 0)
  ) %>%
  # Attach the one valid host identity for each sample AFTER completion.
  # Completing sample and host independently would create invalid pairs.
  left_join(
    analysis_sample_metadata %>% select(sample_id, tentative_species_id),
    by = "sample_id"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SELECT FAMILIES FOR INDIVIDUAL DISPLAY
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Rank using all samples, including zeros, before pooling Families. Larger
# host groups contribute more samples to this whole-dataset ranking.
family_ranking <- sample_family_asvs %>%
  filter(Family_plot != "Unassigned family") %>%
  group_by(Family_plot) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_number_of_asvs = mean(number_of_asvs),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    desc(mean_number_of_asvs),
    Family_plot
  )

top_families <- family_ranking %>%
  slice_head(n = number_of_top_families) %>%
  pull(Family_plot)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# POOL THE REMAINING FAMILIES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Pool within each sample first, so all samples still contribute one
# value (possibly zero) per displayed category to the subsequent mean.
sample_family_asvs_plot <- sample_family_asvs %>%
  mutate(
    Family_plot = case_when(
      Family_plot %in% top_families ~ Family_plot,
      Family_plot == "Unassigned family" ~ "Unassigned family",
      TRUE ~ "Other families"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(sample_id, tentative_species_id, Family_plot) %>%
  summarise(
    number_of_asvs = sum(number_of_asvs),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Use the same display order and colors in both composition plots.
# Grey distinguishes unresolved ASVs and the pooled remaining families.
family_display_levels <- c(
  top_families,
  "Unassigned family",
  "Other families"
)

family_colors <- c(
  setNames(
    grDevices::hcl.colors(max(3, length(top_families)), "Dark 3")[
      seq_along(top_families)
    ],
    top_families
  ),
  "Unassigned family" = "#777777",
  "Other families" = "#D9D9D9"
)

sample_family_asvs_plot <- sample_family_asvs_plot %>%
  mutate(
    Family_plot = factor(Family_plot, levels = family_display_levels)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE MEAN ASV COUNTS WITHIN HOST GROUPS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# The denominator for every Family is now the full host-group sample size.
# The sum of a host's stacked segments equals its mean observed ASV richness.
species_family_composition <- sample_family_asvs_plot %>%
  group_by(tentative_species_id, Family_plot) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_number_of_asvs = mean(number_of_asvs),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
family_composition_plot <- ggplot(
  species_family_composition,
  aes(x = tentative_species_id, y = mean_number_of_asvs, fill = Family_plot)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = family_colors,
    limits = family_display_levels,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = host_levels,
    labels = host_labels
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Web community composition by host-spider species",
    subtitle = "Mean detected ASVs per web sample, grouped by Family",
    x = "Tentative host-spider species",
    y = "Mean ASVs per sample",
    fill = "Family",
    caption = paste0(
      "Display setting: top ",
      length(top_families),
      " named families by mean ASV richness.\n",
      "Unassigned family is separate; remaining named families are pooled as Other families."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.height = grid::unit(0.4, "cm"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )

family_composition_plot
```

```{r hs_family_read_composition, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 7A: FAMILY RELATIVE-READ COMPOSITION BY HOST GROUP
# ============================================================
#
# Main figure: the proportion of retained reads assigned to each Family.
#
# First calculate each Family's percentage within each web sample.
# Then average those percentages equally across all samples in a host
# group, including zeros. Pooling reads before calculating percentages
# would give deeper samples more weight and answer a different question.
# These are sequence-read proportions, not animal counts or biomass.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE FAMILY READ PERCENTAGES WITHIN SAMPLES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
sample_family_reads <- mco_HS_plot_data %>%
  mutate(
    Family_plot = if_else(
      is.na(Family) | str_squish(Family) == "",
      "Unassigned family",
      str_squish(Family)
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(sample_id, Family_plot) %>%
  summarise(
    family_reads = sum(reads),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    sample_id = analysis_sample_metadata$sample_id,
    Family_plot,
    fill = list(family_reads = 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  mutate(
    relative_percent = 100 * family_reads / sum(family_reads)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Pool the same remaining named families within each sample.
# Complete zero categories before joining host IDs, so each sample
# contributes exactly one value to each displayed Family mean.
sample_family_reads_plot <- sample_family_reads %>%
  mutate(
    Family_plot = case_when(
      Family_plot %in% top_families ~ Family_plot,
      Family_plot == "Unassigned family" ~ "Unassigned family",
      TRUE ~ "Other families"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(sample_id, Family_plot) %>%
  summarise(
    relative_percent = sum(relative_percent),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    sample_id = analysis_sample_metadata$sample_id,
    Family_plot = family_display_levels,
    fill = list(relative_percent = 0)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    analysis_sample_metadata %>% select(sample_id, tentative_species_id),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Family_plot = factor(Family_plot, levels = family_display_levels)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# AVERAGE SAMPLE PERCENTAGES WITHIN HOST GROUPS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
species_family_read_composition <- sample_family_reads_plot %>%
  group_by(tentative_species_id, Family_plot) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_relative_percent = mean(relative_percent),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
family_read_composition_plot <- ggplot(
  species_family_read_composition,
  aes(
    x = tentative_species_id,
    y = mean_relative_percent,
    fill = Family_plot
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = family_colors,
    limits = family_display_levels,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = host_levels,
    labels = host_labels
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Family read composition by host-spider species",
    subtitle = "Equal-weight mean of sample-level percentages",
    x = "Tentative host-spider species",
    y = "Mean percentage of retained reads",
    fill = "Family",
    caption = paste(
      "Each bar sums to 100%; categories and colors match the ASV-composition plot.",
      "Read proportions do not directly estimate animal abundance or biomass.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.height = grid::unit(0.4, "cm"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```

```{r hs_sample_family_heatmap, fig.width=14, fig.height=max(8, 4 + 0.23 * nrow(community_matrix) + 0.12 * length(host_levels))}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 7B: FAMILY READ COMPOSITION OF INDIVIDUAL SAMPLES
# ============================================================
#
# Exploratory figure: variation hidden by host-group averages.
#
# Rows are individual samples, grouped by host. Columns use the same
# named families, Unassigned family and Other families as the bars.
# Each cell is the Family's percentage of all retained reads in that
# sample. Every row sums to 100%, including zero detections.
#
# All cells share one percentage scale. The square-root color mapping
# makes low percentages more visible; values and legend labels remain
# actual percentages. No row or column standardization is applied.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# ORDER SAMPLES WITHIN HOST GROUPS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Natural ID order places hw2 before hw10 without changing host order.
sample_family_order <- unlist(
  lapply(host_levels, function(host) {
    str_sort(
      analysis_sample_metadata$sample_id[
        analysis_sample_metadata$tentative_species_id == host
      ],
      numeric = TRUE
    )
  }),
  use.names = FALSE
)

sample_family_heatmap_data <- sample_family_reads_plot %>%
  mutate(
    sample_id = factor(sample_id, levels = rev(sample_family_order))
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
sample_family_heatmap <- ggplot(
  sample_family_heatmap_data,
  aes(x = Family_plot, y = sample_id, fill = relative_percent)
) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_grid(
    tentative_species_id ~ .,
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y",
    switch = "y",
    labeller = labeller(
      tentative_species_id = as_labeller(host_labels)
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = c("#FAFAFA", "#C9DCEC", "#719DC3", "#285B87", "#102940"),
    trans = "sqrt",
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_colorbar(barheight = grid::unit(7, "cm"))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Family read composition of individual web samples",
    subtitle = "Samples grouped by host; shared percentage scale",
    x = "Family",
    y = "Web sample",
    fill = "Retained reads",
    caption = paste(
      "Color uses a square-root scale; labels show actual percentages. Each row sums to 100%.",
      "Unassigned family and Other families have the same definitions as in the composition bars.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.18, "cm"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )

sample_family_heatmap
```

```{r hs_family_detection_heatmap, fig.width=13, fig.height=13}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 7C: FAMILY DETECTION FREQUENCY BY HOST GROUP
# ============================================================
#
# Main figure: how consistently each Family occurs within a host group.
#
# Detection means at least one retained ASV from that Family has reads
# greater than zero. The percentage is detected samples divided by ALL
# samples in the host group, including nondetections.
#
# Show every represented Family, not only the Top N composition set.
# Unassigned family means any unresolved ASV was detected; it is not one
# known shared taxon. A 100% value in an n=1 group represents one sample.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE DETECTION FREQUENCIES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
family_detection_frequency <- sample_family_asvs %>%
  group_by(tentative_species_id, Family_plot) %>%
  summarise(
    detected_samples = sum(number_of_asvs > 0),
    group_samples = n(),
    detection_percent = 100 * mean(number_of_asvs > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Keep the named-Family ranking from the composition plot, followed by
# Unassigned family when present. Split long lists into blocks of 40
# for readable labels; all blocks use the same host order and scale.
full_family_order <- c(
  family_ranking$Family_plot,
  intersect("Unassigned family", sample_family_asvs$Family_plot)
)

family_detection_blocks <- split(
  seq_along(full_family_order),
  ceiling(seq_along(full_family_order) / 40)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
for (family_indices in family_detection_blocks) {

  families_here <- full_family_order[family_indices]

  family_detection_plot_data <- family_detection_frequency %>%
    filter(Family_plot %in% families_here) %>%
    mutate(
      Family_plot = factor(Family_plot, levels = rev(families_here))
    )

  family_detection_plot <- ggplot(
    family_detection_plot_data,
    aes(
      x = tentative_species_id,
      y = Family_plot,
      fill = detection_percent
    )
  ) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      limits = host_levels,
      labels = host_labels,
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = c("#FAFAFA", "#D1E5F0", "#67A9CF", "#2166AC", "#053061"),
      limits = c(0, 100),
      breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
      labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Family detection frequency by host group",
      subtitle = paste0(
        "Family categories ", min(family_indices), "-", max(family_indices),
        " of ", length(full_family_order)
      ),
      x = "Tentative host-spider species",
      y = "Family",
      fill = "Samples detected",
      caption = paste(
        "Percentages use all samples in each host group, including nondetections.",
        "Small groups provide limited evidence about typical occurrence; nondetection is not proof of absence.",
        sep = "\n"
      )
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
    )

  print(family_detection_plot)
}
```

```{r hs_family_upset, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 7D: NAMED-FAMILY SHARING AMONG HOST GROUPS
# ============================================================
#
# Exploratory figure: exact combinations of host groups sharing families.
#
# A Family belongs to a host-group set when at least one sample in
# that group has a positive detection. Filled dots in a column show
# the groups in one exact combination; unmarked groups are excluded.
# The upper bar counts families with exactly that combination.
# Left bars count all named families detected in each host group.
#
# Use all named families, not just the Top N display categories.
# Omit Unassigned family only from this overlap calculation because
# unresolved ASVs do not form one known shared taxon. Those ASVs remain
# in the other analyses. Shared Family labels need not mean shared
# species or ASVs. Group-only detections do not establish specificity.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# BUILD HOST-GROUP PRESENCE SETS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
family_host_presence <- family_detection_frequency %>%
  filter(Family_plot != "Unassigned family") %>%
  transmute(
    Family_plot,
    tentative_species_id,
    present = detected_samples > 0
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = tentative_species_id,
    values_from = present,
    values_fill = FALSE
  ) %>%
  select(Family_plot, all_of(host_levels))

presence_matrix <- family_host_presence %>%
  select(-Family_plot) %>%
  as.matrix()

# Each binary pattern identifies one exact combination of host groups.
# Families are counted once; intersection counts sum to all named families.
family_patterns <- apply(
  presence_matrix,
  1,
  function(x) paste(as.integer(x), collapse = "")
)

upset_intersections <- tibble(
  Family_plot = family_host_presence$Family_plot,
  pattern = family_patterns
) %>%
  group_by(pattern) %>%
  summarise(
    number_of_families = n(),
    families = paste(sort(Family_plot), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(number_of_families), pattern) %>%
  mutate(intersection_id = row_number())

upset_membership <- do.call(
  rbind,
  strsplit(upset_intersections$pattern, "")
) == "1"

upset_set_sizes <- tibble(
  tentative_species_id = host_levels,
  host_position = rev(seq_along(host_levels)),
  number_of_families = as.numeric(colSums(presence_matrix))
)

# Show every observed combination in consecutive blocks of at most 20.
# Host labels, sample sizes and count scales stay the same in every block.
upset_blocks <- split(
  seq_len(nrow(upset_intersections)),
  ceiling(seq_len(nrow(upset_intersections)) / 20)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
for (intersection_indices in upset_blocks) {

  upset_bar_data <- upset_intersections[intersection_indices, ] %>%
    mutate(column_position = row_number())

  upset_matrix_data <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    column_position = seq_along(intersection_indices),
    host_index = seq_along(host_levels)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      host_position = length(host_levels) + 1 - host_index,
      present = upset_membership[
        cbind(intersection_indices[column_position], host_index)
      ]
    )

  upset_lines <- upset_matrix_data %>%
    filter(present) %>%
    group_by(column_position) %>%
    summarise(
      first_host = min(host_position),
      last_host = max(host_position),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Upper bars align with the exact-combination columns below.
  upset_bar_plot <- ggplot(
    upset_bar_data,
    aes(x = column_position, y = number_of_families)
  ) +
    geom_col(fill = "#257C9D", width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = number_of_families), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0.5, nrow(upset_bar_data) + 0.5),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0),
      breaks = NULL
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, max(upset_intersections$number_of_families) * 1.2),
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 4),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Named families") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

  # The left bars show total named-Family detections for each host set.
  upset_set_plot <- ggplot(
    upset_set_sizes,
    aes(x = number_of_families, y = host_position)
  ) +
    geom_col(
      aes(fill = tentative_species_id),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_text(aes(label = number_of_families), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = host_colors) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18)),
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0.5, length(host_levels) + 0.5),
      breaks = rev(seq_along(host_levels)),
      labels = unname(host_labels),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0)
    ) +
    labs(x = "Named families detected", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10)
    )

  # Pale dots are unmarked groups; dark connected dots form one combination.
  upset_matrix_plot <- ggplot(
    upset_matrix_data,
    aes(x = column_position, y = host_position)
  ) +
    geom_point(color = "grey85", size = 2.4) +
    geom_segment(
      data = upset_lines,
      aes(
        x = column_position,
        xend = column_position,
        y = first_host,
        yend = last_host
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = upset_matrix_data %>% filter(present),
      color = "#172C3C",
      size = 2.7
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0.5, nrow(upset_bar_data) + 0.5),
      breaks = upset_bar_data$column_position,
      labels = upset_bar_data$intersection_id,
      expand = expansion(mult = 0)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0.5, length(host_levels) + 0.5),
      breaks = seq_along(host_levels),
      labels = NULL,
      expand = expansion(mult = 0)
    ) +
    labs(x = "Observed combination", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

  # Align the three ggplot panels using grid, which is included with R.
  # Shared widths align upper bars with dots; shared heights align host rows.
  bar_grob <- ggplotGrob(upset_bar_plot)
  set_grob <- ggplotGrob(upset_set_plot)
  matrix_grob <- ggplotGrob(upset_matrix_plot)
  shared_widths <- grid::unit.pmax(bar_grob$widths, matrix_grob$widths)
  bar_grob$widths <- shared_widths
  matrix_grob$widths <- shared_widths
  shared_heights <- grid::unit.pmax(set_grob$heights, matrix_grob$heights)
  set_grob$heights <- shared_heights
  matrix_grob$heights <- shared_heights

  grid::grid.newpage()
  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(
    layout = grid::grid.layout(
      nrow = 4,
      ncol = 2,
      widths = grid::unit(c(5.5, 8.5), "null"),
      heights = grid::unit(c(0.65, 2.0, 4.5, 0.65), "null")
    )
  ))

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 1:2))
  grid::grid.text(
    "Observed Family sharing across host groups",
    y = 0.75,
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 15, fontface = "bold")
  )
  grid::grid.text(
    paste0(
      "Combinations ", min(intersection_indices), "-", max(intersection_indices),
      " of ", nrow(upset_intersections), "; all named families included"
    ),
    y = 0.22,
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 11)
  )
  grid::popViewport()

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 2, layout.pos.col = 2))
  grid::grid.draw(bar_grob)
  grid::popViewport()

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 3, layout.pos.col = 1))
  grid::grid.draw(set_grob)
  grid::popViewport()

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 3, layout.pos.col = 2))
  grid::grid.draw(matrix_grob)
  grid::popViewport()

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 4, layout.pos.col = 1:2))
  grid::grid.text(
    paste(
      "Each column is an exact observed host-group combination; the bar counts named families.",
      "Sampling is unequal. Group-only detections do not establish host specificity.",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 10)
  )
  grid::popViewport(2)
}
```


### D. Beta diversity

```{r hs_nmds, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 8: NMDS OF WEB-COMMUNITY COMPOSITION
# ============================================================
#
# Main figure: community-composition differences.
#
# The existing method is retained: sample-relative ASV reads,
# Bray-Curtis dissimilarity and a two-dimensional NMDS. Each point
# is a web sample. Nearby points represent more similar
# compositions, approximately; inspect stress and convergence before
# interpreting the layout. NMDS axes have no direct biological meaning
# and are not explained-variance percentages. Visual separation is not a
# significance test.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE RELATIVE READS AND BRAY-CURTIS DISTANCES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmds_relative_matrix <- vegan::decostand(
  community_matrix,
  method = "total"
)
bray_curtis_distance <- vegan::vegdist(
  nmds_relative_matrix,
  method = "bray"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# FIT THE TWO-DIMENSIONAL NMDS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(analysis_seed)
# Disable automatic half-change scaling for this dataset.
# This changes coordinate scaling, not stress or input dissimilarities.
mco_HS_nmds <- vegan::metaMDS(
  bray_curtis_distance,
  k = 2,
  trymax = nmds_trymax,
  halfchange = FALSE,
  trace = FALSE
)

# A distance matrix is supplied above, so metaMDS cannot apply another
# transformation to the original counts. Print fitting diagnostics once.

# "Species: scores missing" is expected with a distance-matrix input.
# ASV ordination scores are unavailable; this does not indicate lost data.

mco_HS_nmds

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# EXTRACT SAMPLE COORDINATES AND ATTACH HOST GROUPS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmds_scores <- vegan::scores(mco_HS_nmds, display = "sites") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_id") %>%
  left_join(analysis_sample_metadata, by = "sample_id")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SELECT GROUPS WITH ENOUGH SAMPLES FOR ELLIPSES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Ellipses are descriptive and do not test group differences.
# Require at least four samples; this only controls the ellipse layer.
# All samples, including those in sparse groups, remain visible as points.
ellipse_species <- host_sample_counts %>%
  filter(number_of_samples >= 4) %>%
  pull(tentative_species_id)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmds_plot <- ggplot(
  nmds_scores,
  aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, color = tentative_species_id)
) +
  stat_ellipse(
    data = nmds_scores %>%
      filter(tentative_species_id %in% ellipse_species),
    aes(group = tentative_species_id),
    type = "t",
    level = 0.95,
    linewidth = 0.6,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = host_colors,
    breaks = host_levels,
    labels = host_labels
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "NMDS of spider-web community composition",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Relative reads; Bray-Curtis; stress = ",
      round(mco_HS_nmds$stress, 3)
    ),
    x = "NMDS1",
    y = "NMDS2",
    color = "Tentative host species",
    caption = "Descriptive ellipses shown only for groups with at least four samples."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

nmds_plot
```

```{r hs_nmds_diagnostics}
# ============================================================
# NMDS FIT DIAGNOSTICS: TWO VERSUS THREE DIMENSIONS
# ============================================================
#
# Compare the same Bray-Curtis distances in two and three dimensions.
# More dimensions can reduce distortion. A lower 3D stress is not a
# significance test, and the first two axes of a 3D fit are not a
# replacement for the two-dimensional plot above.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# FIT THE THREE-DIMENSIONAL DIAGNOSTIC
# ------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(analysis_seed)
mco_HS_nmds_3d <- vegan::metaMDS(
  bray_curtis_distance,
  k = 3,
  trymax = nmds_trymax,
  trace = FALSE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SUMMARIZE FIT AND STOPPING INFORMATION
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Repeating the best solution supports stability across random starts;
# it does not prove that a global optimum was found. The stopping
# reason and iteration count below describe the winning start only.
# Inspect them before changing the per-start iteration limit (maxit).
# Increasing random starts does not guarantee an adequate fit.
nmds_models <- list(
  "2D" = mco_HS_nmds,
  "3D" = mco_HS_nmds_3d
)

nmds_stop_reasons <- c(
  "Iteration limit reached",
  "Stress near zero",
  "Stress nearly unchanged",
  "Gradient scale near zero"
)

nmds_fit_summary <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(nmds_models), function(dimension) {
    fit <- nmds_models[[dimension]]
    tibble(
      Dimensions = dimension,
      Stress = fit$stress,
      Starts = fit$tries,
      Repeated = if_else(fit$converged > 0, "Yes", "No"),
      Iterations = fit$iters,
      Stop_reason = nmds_stop_reasons[fit$icause]
    )
  })
)

knitr::kable(
  nmds_fit_summary,
  digits = 4,
  col.names = c("Dimensions", "Stress", "Starts", "Best repeated", "Iterations", "Stop reason")
)
```

```{r hs_nmds_shepard, fig.width=13, fig.height=6}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 8A: NMDS SHEPARD DIAGNOSTICS
# ============================================================
#
# The x-axis shows observed Bray-Curtis dissimilarity. The y-axis
# shows distance in the fitted ordination. Scatter around the fitted
# monotone line indicates distortion; inspect this together with stress.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# stressplot supplies its own x-axis and y-axis titles. Do not pass
# xlab or ylab again, because duplicate arguments stop knitting.
previous_par <- par(
  mfrow = c(1, 2),
  mar = c(4.5, 4.8, 3.5, 1)
)

for (dimension in names(nmds_models)) {
  vegan::stressplot(
    nmds_models[[dimension]],
    pch = 16,
    p.col = "#257C9D",
    cex = 0.55
  )
  title(main = paste(dimension, "NMDS Shepard plot"))
}

par(previous_par)
```
